title: Scalar reduction of the normalized diagonal DNC factor
statement: Fix the finite purity conventions [def-pur-conventions] and the actual comparisons [def-pur-finite-diagonal-reduction-comparisons]. Let f:X to Y be separated, quasi-compact, locally of finite type and smooth of pure relative dimension d over the algebraically closed base field k, with Y separated of finite type. Let A=A_E,n and B=A_E,m for 1<=m<=n, and Q be derived scalar extension. Use the source and normal sections of the diagonal and the root-line conventions [def-coefficient-twists-detailed]. The normalized DNC factor delta_R: C_R(p1,Delta) to C_R(pi,z) satisfies q_N Q(delta_A)=delta_B q_C. The compared coefficient maps are the actual exceptional and pullback mates on the diagonal and normal sections. Identity reductions, d=0, empty schemes and arbitrary ramification are included.

proof.text:
use centred etale coordinates near the diagonal. The support-restriction
and normal-coordinate maps are exceptional mates and hence commute with scalar
extension by pullback balancing and reduced-counit compatibility. The normal frame
maps the coefficient-independent class of y_i-x_i to d x_i. In every such chart,
conjugating the reduced DNC map by its two section coefficient comparisons has
identity standard reading: the original DNC map does, and both coordinate squares
commute. Coordinate normalization and uniqueness of DNC invariance therefore give
the DNC map at the reduced level. Etale locality glues the equality globally.
The empty coordinate frame gives the same argument when d=0.
